This seems like undesirable behaviour. Your reproduction steps describes precisely what I would do if I had initially accidentally typed my input in the wrong session. Upon accidentally typing input into the wrong session, it is convenient to be able to easily carry that input over to the correct session.

For anyone who doesn't want to wait for a proper fix and would like to clean up the sidebar right now — here's a workaround script (AI-assisted) that I've been using:

https://gist.github.com/azkore/807e5736aad043ad5d442acb686140cd

**How it works:** As described in the issue, the sidebar is driven by snapshot tree hashes stored in `step-start`/`step-finish` parts, not by actual git state. The script clears those stale snapshot references and injects a fresh baseline (`HEAD` tree → current working tree) that `computeDiff` treats as native. After running it, the sidebar reflects real uncommitted changes — and stays correct through subsequent prompts because the injected `step-start` anchors `from` to `HEAD`.

**Heads up:** This directly mutates the OpenCode DB and snapshot data. Works great for me but please back up your DB (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) before trying it. Best run while the session is idle.

Usage: `oc-refresh-diff <session-id>`

I prefer sandboxing only the agent shell commands, since it's easier to be more restrictive (i.e. no network access). It's currently possible by writing a custom shell wrapper and running opencode with `SHELL=/path/to/restricted-bash` environment variable.

It may be possible to wrap bash in the Anthropic's sandbox-runtime or anything. For example, I use this simple bubblewrap sandbox:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

REPO_DIR="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

bwrap --die-with-parent \
      --unshare-all \
      --hostname AGENT_SANDBOX \
      --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --tmpfs /run/ --tmpfs /tmp/ --proc /proc \
      --ro-bind /run/systemd/resolve/ /run/systemd/resolve/ \
      --tmpfs /home \
      --overlay-src ~/.config --tmp-overlay ~/.config \
      --overlay-src ~/.cargo --tmp-overlay ~/.cargo \
      --overlay-src ~/.rustup --tmp-overlay ~/.rustup \
      --bind "$REPO_DIR" "$REPO_DIR" \
      --ro-bind "$REPO_DIR/.git" "$REPO_DIR/.git" \
      --chdir "$PWD" \
      bash "$@"

```

* no network access (`--unshare-net`)
* write access to the current working directory, except for `.git` (so I can reliably check what has changed)
* read-only access to listed directories, in this example its ~/.config, ~/.cargo, ~/.rustup
* always has access to the entire repository, regardless of the bash tool set working directory

However, this is still not bulletproof, just a simple measure against agent fetching some prompt-injected content and downloading malware. (anything in the directory may be poisoned, so I'd need to run `git clean -xfd` before I do anything in the repo outside of opencode)

I just always have to start opencode with `SHELL=~/utils/agent-shell opencode`.
I'd appreciate if it was possible to set the shell permanently in ~/.config/opencode.
Adding such sandbox by default isn't necessarily a good idea IMHO, since it may provide false sense of security :/

I’m seeing a very similar underlying state to what @odiiiiiiii described above, but on Linux/WSL and not necessarily tied to the “collapse” itself.

## What I’m seeing (concrete evidence)

For a git project directory:
`opencode-unstuck-session-plugin`

The DB still contains sessions for that directory, but most of them are still associated to `project_id = "global"`:

- total sessions with `directory == -unstuck-session-plugin`: 57
- of those, `project_id = global`: 54
  - root sessions (parent_id IS NULL) under `global`: 4
- `project_id = c126a4a9234ab5ca8ab63c07390286fdd2f3aa2c`: 3 (all are child sessions)

The server resolves the directory to a non-global git project id:
- `GET /project/current?directory=-unstuck-session-plugin` -> `id=c126a4...`

But session listing for that directory then shows “no sessions” because the root sessions are still under `global`:
- `GET /session?directory=-unstuck-session-plugin&roots=true&limit=200` -> `[]`

So the data isn’t gone — it’s split between `global` and the per-project id, and the `global` portion becomes invisible once the instance is scoped to the non-global project id.

## How this relates to the crash scenario
A crash may be one way to end up in this state (migration interrupted/failed), but the same symptom can occur even without a crash if global->project migration never ran for a worktree that already has a project row (or if it failed at some point).

## Suggestion / fix direction
In addition to any worktree-id repair work, I think opencode needs a safe repair/migration path for legacy `global` sessions:

- If a git-backed project id is resolved for a worktree, and there exist sessions with `project_id='global'` that belong to that worktree (e.g. `session.directory == project.worktree`), migrate them to the canonical project id (similar to what @odiiiiiiii’s agent did).
- This should be done with a DB backup + transaction, and ideally run once (or only when such sessions are detected).

This would prevent the “sessions disappeared” symptom where sessions still exist in the DB but are stuck under `global` and no longer show up in `/session` for that project.
